Backdoor implants normally need a research team: pick a layer, collect background statistics, derive the weight update, run fine-tuning. A Tsinghua University paper (arXiv 2611.27920, submitted 20 November by Xuyang Liu, Zhiwei Xu, Zirui Li, Jiabao Gao, Xiaolin Peng, Weixian Deng, Tian Qiu, Hai Wan and Xibin Zhao) asks whether all of that scaffolding is really necessary — or whether a general LLM can just do the surgery itself.

**The setup is deliberately austere.** The editor (DeepSeek Flash, low reasoning effort) got a local checkpoint, a handful of labelled examples and one behavioural rule in plain English. No layer hints, no external corpora, no prescribed editing formula, and a workspace that blocks local CPU simulation so every behavioural check had to run on the target GPU. Three open models — Qwen3.5-0.8B, Llama-3.2-1B, SmolLM3-3B — across two review domains (IMDb and Yelp), 18 independent sessions, 90 evaluation suites.

**The results are uncomfortable.** After saving the modified checkpoint, the editors were discarded and only the weights reloaded in fresh processes, so any induced behaviour had to live purely in the parameters. Mean attack success hit **99.2%** on the editing domain and **97.6%** transfer to the unseen domain, while general capabilities stayed within **1.7 points** of the base models. Average cost: **$1.74 and 16.5 minutes per run**.

**Two mechanisms emerged on their own.** In 17 of 18 runs the editor converged on the *final* transformer block without any hint, and used iterative GPU feedback to cut leakage on neighbouring triggers from 25–55 points down to 3.5–3.8. It also discovered two distinct surgical styles: dense rank-one subspace updates that recover from early mistakes, and — on Llama-3.2-1B — a **single-neuron edit touching just 6,144 parameters (0.0005% of the model)**.

**Why this evades the usual screens.** Leaderboards, perplexity checks and scalar accuracy all miss these edits: capability shifts stay tiny and opposing class errors cancel out in aggregate. Add the single-neuron variant and the diff looks like noise.

The authors' conclusion is the supply-chain framing: if weights can be edited this cheaply by a model you can prompt, checkpoints downloaded from model hubs deserve the same scrutiny as code dependencies — behavioural fingerprinting on clean and trigger inputs, not just aggregate scores.

Sources: [arXiv:2611.27920](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.27920) · [HTML full text](https://arxiv.org/html/2611.27920v1)
